Classroom: student panels with the teacher as lead judge; the second audience is another class, staff, or the history capstone's outside venue (also meets D4.3.9-12, audiences outside the classroom). Home: the parent is the live first audience and lead judge; the second audience is a real listener outside the home, chosen from a menu (a relative or family friend live by phone or video; a library, co-op or community group; or a public written venue such as a letter to a local official or a public comment). Fallback: two contrasting forms to two outside audiences, the parent giving live questions. Quality held equal by the same rubric rows, a planning sheet showing what changed between audiences (the SL.11-12.6 evidence), and a short reflection. Safety: student-chosen and parent-approved; Curio Class collects and posts nothing. One shared outside audience serves ELA 12 unit 8 and US History II unit 12.
